subject: [bsp/gd32] add gd32h759i-eval bsp add fix drv_usart.c (#10623)
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit message is "[bsp/gd32] add gd32h759i-eval bsp add fix drv_usart.c", and its change to the arm drv_usart.c adds a whole new UART DMA receive/transmit path (gd32_dma_config, gd32_dma_tx_config, gd32_dma_transmit, DMA IRQ handlers) gated on RT_SERIAL_USING_DMA / RT_SERIAL_USING_TX_DMA, which the arm drv_usart.h undefines unless the chip is a GD32H7xx part. The two picked hunks only wire up that new feature: they put .dma_transmit = gd32_dma_transmit into the ops table and OR RT_DEVICE_FLAG_DMA_RX/TX into the registration flags when DMA is configured; with DMA not configured the result is the same as before (NULL instead of RT_NULL, and the same RDWR | INT_RX flags). The risc-v drv_usart.c has no DMA code at all (no DMA functions, no DMA fields in its uart struct), so its RT_NULL ops slot and RDWR | INT_RX registration are correct for that driver. This is a feature addition, not a bug fix.

subject: [bsp][n32] n32hxxx: add the H47x_48x/H49x timer support and cover the BSP with ci-attach
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit message says it adds "the H47x_48x/H49x timer support" and that "drv_pwm.c and drv_pulse_encoder.c are extended to the H47x_48x/H49x instances"; the bug fixes it lists are in drv_nand.c and timer_ctrl(), not in drv_pwm.c. The first picked hunk replaces MAX_PERIOD with pwm_max_period_get(), which still returns MAX_PERIOD (65535) for every timer except GTIM1-4 under SOC_SERIES_N32H49x, where it returns 0xFFFFFFFF so the newly supported series can use its wider counter; for all previously supported timers the result is unchanged, and keeping ARR within 65535 is still a valid setting, so this extends the driver rather than correcting it. The second picked hunk wraps the PWM4 channel setup in #if defined(SOC_SERIES_N32H7xx) because only the n32 H7xx pwm_config.h defines a PWM4 (ATIM4) instance, and the same commit guards the PWM4 enum and table entries the same way. The at32 drv_pwm.c has no n32 series split: its PWM4_INDEX and BSP_USING_PWM3_CH4/PWM4_CHx lines match only as text, and its psc = period / MAX_PERIOD + 1 keeps ARR within 16 bits, consistent with its own MAX_PERIOD of 65535.

subject: [bsp][n32] n32hxxx: add the H47x_48x/H49x timer support and cover the BSP with ci-attach
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit message says it adds "the H47x_48x/H49x timer support" and that "drv_pwm.c and drv_pulse_encoder.c are extended to the H47x_48x/H49x instances"; the bug fixes it lists are in drv_nand.c and timer_ctrl(), not in drv_pwm.c. The three picked hunks all serve that extension: the first replaces an N32H7xx-only comment with N32_PWM_CMP_VALUE(), which casts to uint32_t only under SOC_SERIES_N32H49x and keeps the old uint16_t cast otherwise (the stm32 lines it matched are just the MIN_PERIOD/MIN_PULSE context); the second replaces MAX_PERIOD with pwm_max_period_get(), which still returns MAX_PERIOD for every timer except GTIM1-4 under SOC_SERIES_N32H49x; the third wraps the PWM4 channel setup in #if defined(SOC_SERIES_N32H7xx) because only the n32 H7xx pwm_config.h defines a PWM4 (ATIM4) instance. The stm32 drv_pwm.c has no n32 series split, writes the compare value through __HAL_TIM_SET_COMPARE without a 16-bit cast, and its psc = period / MAX_PERIOD + 1 is consistent with its own MAX_PERIOD of 65535.

subject: fix:[stm32][lcd]Error in control call of lcd test function (#10040)
label: missing
evidence: The fix (title "Error in control call of lcd test function", body "Optimize the lcd_test function to call it in thread to prevent the CLI environment from being unavailable after execution") turned the stm32 lcd_test, an MSH command that looks up the "lcd" device and then loops forever, into a thread entry lcd_thread that a new lcd_test starts with rt_thread_create, and replaced lcd->parent.control with rt_device_control; the picked hunk is the start of the thread part. msh runs a command by calling it directly (*retp = cmd_func(argc, argv) in msh.c), so a command that never returns blocks the shell. In the ArtPi drv_spi_ili9488.c, ili9488_test is the same logic: it looks up "lcd" with rt_device_find (lines 1097-1098), draws some test content, then enters while (1) filling the framebuffer and calling lcd->parent.control with RTGRAPHIC_CTRL_RECT_UPDATE, and it is exported with MSH_CMD_EXPORT, so it never returns to the shell; nothing in the file starts it in its own thread, and DRV_DEBUG is defined in the file itself. The fix needs no hardware feature, and the same function also keeps the other half of the problem (not picked because the text differs): its lcd->parent.control calls cannot compile when RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS is on, because rtdef.h only declares the control member when that option is off, while this driver supports the option (device->ops = &lcd_ops). Only a debug shell command is affected.
impact_note: Only the ili9488_test debug shell command is affected: running it never returns and leaves the msh shell unusable until reset (and its direct control calls break the build only with the non-default RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS option); normal LCD operation is unchanged.
title: The ArtPi ILI9488 test shell command runs an endless drawing loop in the shell thread, so the shell is unusable after it is run.
summary: On 2025-02-27, commit 50683295 changed lcd_test in the stm32 HAL drv_lcd.c so that its endless red/green/blue loop runs in its own thread (lcd_thread) and the shell command returns at once, and switched its screen-update calls to rt_device_control. The ArtPi drv_spi_ili9488.c has the same kind of test command, ili9488_test, which still looks up the "lcd" device and then loops forever in the caller's thread. If it is not fixed, running ili9488_test from msh blocks the shell until the board is reset; its lcd->parent.control calls also do not compile if RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS is enabled. The port needs rewriting rather than copying, because ili9488_test draws images and text before its loop and passes a rect_info argument, so the stack size for the new thread (256 bytes in the stm32 fix) must be checked; BSP_USING_SPI_LCD_ILI9488 is off in the board's default rtconfig.h.

subject: fix:[stm32][lcd]Error in control call of lcd test function (#10040)
label: missing
evidence: The fix (title "Error in control call of lcd test function", body "Optimize the lcd_test function to call it in thread to prevent the CLI environment from being unavailable after execution") turned the stm32 lcd_test, an MSH command that looks up the "lcd" device and then loops forever, into a thread entry lcd_thread that a new lcd_test starts with rt_thread_create after a NULL check, and replaced every lcd->parent.control call with rt_device_control. The WeAct drv_lcd_spi.c lcd_test is the same logic as the pre-fix code: the same rt_device_find lookup with no NULL check, a while (1) red/green/blue framebuffer fill, lcd->parent.control with RTGRAPHIC_CTRL_RECT_UPDATE after each color, and MSH_CMD_EXPORT(lcd_test, lcd_test); it only lacks the RGB888 branch, so the two RGB888-branch hunks have no separate counterpart while the other hunks map one to one. Because msh calls the command directly (*retp = cmd_func(argc, argv) in msh.c), the loop blocks the shell; and because rtdef.h declares the control member of struct rt_device only when RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS is off while this driver supports that option (device->ops = &lcd_ops), the direct calls cannot compile with it, whereas rt_device_control dispatches through dev->ops. The file defines DRV_DEBUG itself, nothing on this side runs the test in its own thread or uses another call path, and the fix depends on no hardware feature.
impact_note: Only the lcd_test debug shell command is affected: running it never returns and leaves the msh shell unusable until reset, and its direct control calls break the build only with the non-default RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS option; normal LCD operation is unchanged.
title: The WeAct H750 lcd_test shell command still runs its endless loop in the shell thread and calls lcd->parent.control directly, the two problems fixed in the stm32 drv_lcd.c.
summary: On 2025-02-27, commit 50683295 fixed lcd_test in bsp/stm32/libraries/HAL_Drivers/drivers/drv_lcd.c: the endless red/green/blue loop now runs in its own thread started by a new lcd_test that also checks the device lookup, and the screen-update calls go through rt_device_control. The WeAct board's drv_lcd_spi.c is a copy of the old code: its lcd_test looks up "lcd", loops forever in the caller's thread, calls lcd->parent.control three times and has no NULL check. If it is not fixed, running lcd_test from msh blocks the shell until the board is reset, and enabling RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS makes this file fail to compile because struct rt_device then has no control member. The command is built by default on this board (BSP_USING_LCD_SPI and FINSH_USING_MSH are set in its rtconfig.h), but only a debug command is affected.

subject: fix:[stm32][lcd]Error in control call of lcd test function (#10040)
label: missing
evidence: The fix has two parts: the stm32 lcd_test endless loop was moved into its own thread (commit body: "Optimize the lcd_test function to call it in thread to prevent the CLI environment from being unavailable after execution"), and every lcd->parent.control call was replaced with rt_device_control (title: "Error in control call of lcd test function"). The thread part (the first hunk and the new lcd_test in the last hunk) does not apply here: the tkm32F499 lcd_test fills red, green and blue once each and returns 0, and it already checks the rt_device_find result for RT_NULL. The control-call hunks do apply: lcd_test (lines 272, 279, 286) and the non-debug helper Lcd_ColorBox (line 159) call lcd->parent.control directly, while this driver supports RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS (device->ops = &lcd_ops) and rtdef.h declares the control member of struct rt_device only when that option is off, so the file cannot compile with it, the same failure the stm32 lcd_test had; rt_device_control dispatches through dev->ops in that configuration. RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS is an ordinary kernel option in src/Kconfig (default n), so this is a build failure in a non-default configuration; under the build-error convention it is judged missing, with light impact.
impact_note: The direct lcd->parent.control calls only break the build when the non-default RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS option is enabled; in the default configuration they behave the same as rt_device_control.
title: The tkm32F499 LCD driver calls lcd->parent.control directly, which does not compile when RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS is enabled; the stm32 drv_lcd.c fix replaced the same call with rt_device_control.
summary: On 2025-02-27, commit 50683295 fixed the stm32 drv_lcd.c test command by replacing its direct lcd->parent.control calls with rt_device_control and by moving its endless loop into a separate thread. The tkm32F499 drv_lcd.c still calls lcd->parent.control in Lcd_ColorBox, which is built whenever BSP_USING_LCD is set, and three times in lcd_test, although the driver itself has an RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS registration path; struct rt_device has no control member in that configuration, so the file fails to compile there. The thread part of the fix does not apply, because this lcd_test draws each color once and returns, and it already checks the device lookup for NULL. If it is not fixed, the only effect is that this LCD driver cannot be built with RT_USING_DEVICE_OPS enabled (default off); BSP_USING_LCD is also off in the board's default rtconfig.h.

subject: [bsp][drv_gpio] fix the error code return when pin number is illegal
label: missing
evidence: The commit "[bsp][drv_gpio] fix the error code return when pin number is illegal" changed pin_read in about 50 BSP GPIO drivers so that an unknown pin returns -RT_EINVAL instead of a pin level; in the gd32 risc-v driver the picked hunk turns "return value;" (value preset to PIN_LOW) into "return -RT_EINVAL;" after get_pin() returns RT_NULL. The ht32 drv_gpio.c ht32_pin_read is the same pre-fix logic: it presets value = PIN_LOW, calls get_pin(pin), and on RT_NULL returns value, so an illegal pin reads as low and the caller cannot see the error. Its return type is already rt_ssize_t, the same as the pin_read op in dev_pin.h and rt_pin_read, which passes the driver's value straight back, so nothing prevents returning -RT_EINVAL; the fix uses no hardware feature. The other lines the script matched (get_pin checks in pin_mode, pin_write and the irq functions) are only shared lookup context; the fix concerns the return value in pin_read. The ht32 driver was added on 2024-04-17, after the 2024-03-24 fix, and has not been changed since.

evidence_refs.quote: static rt_ssize_t ht32_pin_read(rt_device_t dev, rt_base_t pin)

impact_note: Only reads of a pin number that is not in the pin table are affected: they report PIN_LOW instead of returning -RT_EINVAL, so callers that pass valid pins see no change.
title: The HT32 GPIO driver returns PIN_LOW instead of an error code when asked to read an illegal pin number.
summary: On 2024-03-24, commit 6a9c42a1 changed pin_read in about 50 BSP GPIO drivers, including the gd32 risc-v one, so that an illegal pin number returns -RT_EINVAL instead of a pin level. The HT32 BSP was added on 2024-04-17 with ht32_pin_read still written the old way: when get_pin() finds no entry it returns the preset PIN_LOW. If it is not fixed, rt_pin_read on an invalid pin silently reports a low level, and callers cannot tell a wrong pin number from a real low input. The change is one line and uses nothing specific to the HT32 hardware.

subject: [bsp][nxp][mcxa153] fix compiling problem
label: not_applicable
evidence: The commit "[bsp][nxp][mcxa153] fix compiling problem" renamed the driver's own DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_COUNT (32767) to DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE in the mcxa drv_spi.c; at that commit the MCXA153 SDK header fsl_lpspi_edma.h (driver version 2.4.4), which drv_spi.c includes just before its definition, itself defines DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_COUNT 0x7FFFU, so the rename only removes that name clash and changes no value (0x7FFF = 32767). The mcxn drv_spi.c has the same include and definition (lines 14 and 16), but the MCXN236 and MCXN947 copies of fsl_lpspi_edma.h that the repository held (driver version 2.0.0 at the fix commit, 2.1.0 and 2.1.1 up to commit 27430ca7, which moved the SDK out of the tree in 2025-05) do not define DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_COUNT, so on mcxn the macro clashes with nothing. The problem therefore comes from the SDK version used for the MCXA153 part, not from the shared driver logic. At the pinned commit both BSPs take the SDK from the external package selected by PKG_USING_NXP_MCX_SERIES_DRIVER (version "latest"), which the repository does not hold, so the current MCXN header cannot be checked and confidence is only medium; even if a newer header defined the macro, its value would be the same 32767 and nothing at run time would change.

subject: [BSP][NXP] Add new features of I2C DMA, CAN, SPI, DWT and SDIO for RT1180 (#11715)
label: not_applicable
evidence: The hunk un-comments the 0x20000000-0x20080000 range in the bounce-buffer condition of _mmc_request, so that buffers in i.MX RT tightly coupled memory are copied through an aligned heap buffer before USDHC DMA; the fixed line's comment gives the reason: 'DTCM/System TCM - not DMA-accessible'. The imx6ull-smart copy still has this range commented out at line 464 in the same function, but this BSP (ARCH_ARM_CORTEX_A7 with MMU) has no TCM at that address: board.h documents the memory map as OCRAM at 0x0090_0000 plus peripheral blocks at 0x0200_0000-0x022F_FFFF, and board.c maps 0x00000000-0x80000000 as DEVICE_MEM with normal memory only from 0x80000000 (or from KERNEL_VADDR_START 0xc0000000 under RT_USING_SMART). The system heap is set up in DDR between __bss_end and HEAP_END (0x80000000 + 64 MB, or KERNEL_VADDR_START + 16 MB), so no data buffer is expected in the 0x20000000 window the fix targets. The fix depends on the i.MX RT TCM address layout, which this board does not have; the ITCM check that is already present there is likewise a leftover from the i.MX RT driver.

subject: [BSP][NXP] Add new features of I2C DMA, CAN, SPI, DWT and SDIO for RT1180 (#11715)
label: missing
evidence: The picked hunks change '1 << i' and '1 << index' to '1U << i' and '1U << index' in the RT_CAN_CMD_SET_FILTER branch of can_control; the commit message bullet says 'fix: use unsigned shift to avoid UB in drv_can.c'. The bit index runs from 0 to 31 (comment 'hdr index 0~31 map RX MB index 1~32'), and shifting the int constant 1 into bit 31 is undefined behaviour in C, which the unsigned literal avoids. The mcxn copy has the same can_control filter code with the same static rt_uint32_t filter_mask bitmap, the same 0..31 search loop at line 250, and the unchanged signed shifts at lines 252 and 276 (plus line 261 for a user-given hdr_bank, which the source commit also changed); nothing in the copy keeps the index below 31 before shifting, and the CAN core passes the filter request to the driver before any hdr_bank range check. The fix needs only a 1U literal, so no hardware or SDK dependency could make it inapplicable; with common compilers the signed shift still yields 0x80000000, so the runtime result most likely stays the same.

evidence_refs.quote: /* RX MB index from 1 to 32,hdr index 0~31 map RX MB index 1~32. */

impact_note: Shifting 1 into bit 31 of a signed int is undefined in C, but common compilers produce 0x80000000, so the filter bitmap most likely behaves the same once fixed.
title: The MCXN CAN driver tracks used filter slots with signed shifts (1 << i, 1 << index), which are undefined in C when the slot index reaches 31.
summary: On 2026-08-21 commit 6ea68279 changed the i.MX RT CAN driver to use unsigned shifts (1U << i, 1U << index, 1U << item->hdr_bank) when it records which receive mailboxes already have a filter, to avoid undefined behaviour. The MCXN CAN driver is a copy of the same filter code and still uses 1 << i and 1 << index at lines 252 and 276, and 1 << item->hdr_bank at line 261. When filter slot 31 is searched or used, the shift moves a 1 into the sign bit of an int, which C leaves undefined; in practice compilers give 0x80000000, so filters most likely keep working. The same one-character change per line carries over unchanged.

subject: bsp: fm33lc026: Fix GPIO IRQ map lookup
label: not_applicable
evidence: The picked hunk changes the PIN_IRQ_DISABLE branch of fm33_pin_irq_enable from get_pin_irq_map(PIN_STPIN(pin)) to get_pin_irq_map(pin); the commit message says 'Pass encoded pin values to the IRQ map lookup path'. That is right for fm33lc026 because its get_pin_irq_map(rt_base_t pin) calls pin2irqindex(pin), which compares the encoded pin number against a pin_irq_map that holds encoded pin numbers such as {3, FL_GPIO_EXTI_LINE_0}. In the n32hxxx driver, get_pin_irq_map(uint32_t pinbit) instead calls bit2bitno(pinbit), and its pin_irq_map is indexed by pin bit position ({ GPIO_PIN_0, EXTI_LINE0, EXTI0_IRQn }, ...), so it expects the bit mask that PIN_STPIN(pin) produces; the enable branch of the same function also uses bit2bitno(PIN_STPIN(pin)). Line 397 only has the same text as the pre-fix fm33lc026 line, not the same logic: there PIN_STPIN(pin) is the correct argument, and passing the encoded pin would break the lookup.

subject: [bsp/nxp/mcx/mcxa] Fix UART clock configuration type mismatch
label: missing
evidence: The picked hunk replaces kLPUART_RxDataRegFullInterruptEnable with kLPUART_RxDataRegFullFlag in mcx_getc, where the constant is ANDed with the value returned by LPUART_GetStatusFlags(); the commit message lists 'Fix mcx_getc() to use correct status flag kLPUART_RxDataRegFullFlag'. The mcxe copy has the identical mcx_getc check at line 163, and elsewhere uses kLPUART_RxDataRegFullInterruptEnable as an interrupt-enable mask (lines 136 and 141), so testing the status word with it is the same mistake; the status-flag constants the fix relies on are already used by the mcxe driver (kLPUART_TxDataRegEmptyFlag in mcx_putc at line 153), so nothing makes the fix inapplicable. The MCX SDK header comes from an external package (CONFIG_PKG_USING_NXP_MCX_SERIES_DRIVER=y) and is not in the repository; the only in-tree NXP LPUART header (imx91 SDK) defines the enable constant as LPUART_CTRL_RIE_MASK and the flag as LPUART_STAT_RDRF_MASK and documents both as bit 21, so the old check most likely tests the right bit by coincidence and the runtime result most likely stays the same.

evidence_refs.quote: kLPUART_RxDataRegFullInterruptEnable = (LPUART_CTRL_RIE_MASK), /*!< Receiver data register full. bit 21 */

impact_note: The in-tree NXP LPUART header documents both constants as bit 21, so the wrong constant most likely tests the same status bit; the MCX SDK header itself is not in the repository to confirm this.
title: The MCXE UART driver's mcx_getc checks for received data with the interrupt-enable constant kLPUART_RxDataRegFullInterruptEnable instead of the status flag kLPUART_RxDataRegFullFlag.
summary: On 2025-10-21 commit 982e52e2 fixed the MCXA UART driver so that mcx_getc tests the receive status with the status flag kLPUART_RxDataRegFullFlag instead of the interrupt-enable constant kLPUART_RxDataRegFullInterruptEnable. The MCXE UART driver is a copy of that code and still has the old check at line 163. In the NXP LPUART header that is in the repository (imx91 SDK) both constants are documented as bit 21, so the check most likely works by coincidence today; if the MCX SDK gave them different values, mcx_getc would miss received bytes or read when nothing has arrived. The MCX SDK comes from an external package that is not in the repository, so the values for MCXE could not be confirmed. The fix is a one-word replacement.

subject: fix: resolve QSPI compilation error and add CI guard for stm32l475-atk-pandora
label: missing
evidence: The picked hunk replaces the plain assignments 'qspi_device->enter_qspi_mode = enter_qspi_mode;' and 'qspi_device->exit_qspi_mode = exit_qspi_mode;' in rt_hw_qspi_device_attach with explicit casts to void (*)(struct rt_qspi_device *); the commit message says 'fix: resolve QSPI compilation error' and 'Fix function pointer type mismatch between drv_qspi.h and rt_qspi_device'. The at32 driver has the same function with the same parameter types void (*enter_qspi_mode)() and void (*exit_qspi_mode)() (drv_qspi.c line 426, drv_qspi.h line 36) and stores them without a cast at lines 443-444 into struct rt_qspi_device members declared as void (*enter_qspi_mode)(struct rt_qspi_device *device) in dev_spi.h, so it has exactly the mismatch the commit names. With a compiler that treats '()' as '(void)', as C23 does, these assignments are between incompatible pointer types, so the toolchain that broke the STM32 file would also break this file whenever BSP_USING_QSPI is enabled (offered in the at32f435/437/455/456/457 board Kconfig); both BSP families build with GCC without an explicit -std flag. The fix needs nothing hardware-specific; only the build is affected, not the generated code.
impact_note: Only decides whether drv_qspi.c compiles with a compiler that rejects the mismatched function-pointer assignment; the stored callback and runtime behaviour are the same.
title: The AT32 QSPI driver stores the enter/exit QSPI-mode callbacks, declared as void (*)(), into rt_qspi_device members of type void (*)(struct rt_qspi_device *) without a cast, the same mismatch that broke the STM32 QSPI build.
summary: On 2025-12-17 commit 99a25459 fixed a QSPI compilation error in the STM32 driver by casting the enter_qspi_mode and exit_qspi_mode callbacks to void (*)(struct rt_qspi_device *) before storing them in struct rt_qspi_device. The AT32 QSPI driver has the same rt_hw_qspi_device_attach with the same void (*)() parameters and still stores them without a cast at lines 443-444. With a compiler that treats '()' as '(void)', as C23 does, these are incompatible pointer assignments, so enabling BSP_USING_QSPI on an AT32 board would most likely fail to build with the same toolchain that broke the STM32 build. Runtime behaviour does not change; the exact compiler from issue #11036 is not visible in the repository.

subject: [bsp/stm32]fix compile warning (#10108)

subject: fix[stm32[SDMMC]: Optimize SDMMC timeout handling and clock divider
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The picked hunks are (1) a new helper stm32_sdio_clk_get() that returns SDIO_CLOCK_FREQ, which the fixed driver only uses as a fallback when the descriptor's clk_get pointer is NULL, and (2)/(3) a swap of the whole-cache SCB_CleanInvalidateDCache() for buffer-range rt_hw_cpu_dcache_ops() calls on cache_buf around the IDMA transfer. Neither corrects a behavioural error: RT_HW_CACHE_FLUSH maps to SCB_CleanDCache_by_Addr on cache_buf, so the old whole-cache clean+invalidate already covered everything the new range calls do and the change only narrows cache maintenance (a speed-up), and the commit message ("Optimize SDMMC timeout handling and clock divider") does not mention cache handling at all. The helper has nothing to attach to here: this driver's rthw_sdio_iocfg() never calls a clk_get pointer and takes the clock directly from SDIO_CLOCK_FREQ. The commit's timeout and divider changes are not among the picked hunks; this driver already rounds the divider up (line 334) and keeps a loop-count data wait (line 221), which this candidate does not cover.

label: missing
evidence: The picked hunks change the PM callbacks wdt_pm_suspend, wdt_pm_frequency_change and usbhost_pm_suspend from int to rt_err_t (commit message: "Fix compilation issues with bsp of nuvoton series") and move the opening brace of the NU_USBHOST_MUTEX_INIT/LOCK/UNLOCK macros to the next line, which is formatting only. The return-type part is a build fix: since bceb6635 (July 2024) struct rt_device_pm_ops declares suspend and frequency_change as rt_err_t (pm.h lines 138 and 140), rt_err_t is rt_base_t, i.e. rt_int32_t, which is int32_t in GCC builds because the newlib SConscript defines RT_USING_LIBC, so it need not be int, and initializing these members with int-returning functions is an incompatible function-pointer initialization. The nuc980 drv_wdt.c (prototypes at lines 62 and 64, definitions at 93 and 141, stored at lines 83 and 85) and drv_usbhost.c (line 893, stored at line 940) still have exactly the pre-fix int callbacks inside the same RT_USING_PM blocks, so a nuc980 build with RT_USING_PM on gets the same diagnostic the commit removed from m480 (fixed forms at m480 drv_wdt.c lines 132 and 184); the nuc980 boards build with the same arm-none-eabi GCC and nothing chip-specific is involved. Every callback returns (int)RT_EOK, so run-time behaviour is the same, the shipped nk-980iot config leaves RT_USING_PM off, the nuc980 Kconfig has no option that selects it and no nuc980 drv_*.c calls rt_system_pm_init, and the repository does not show whether the original diagnostic was an error or only a warning, hence medium confidence and light impact.

title: The NUC980 watchdog and USB host drivers still declare their PM callbacks as returning int, while struct rt_device_pm_ops now expects rt_err_t, so a build with RT_USING_PM gets the incompatible function-pointer initialization that commit e7e44ec fixed in the m031, m2354 and m480 copies.
summary: On 2024-09-29 commit e7e44ec ("Fix compilation issues with bsp of nuvoton series") changed wdt_pm_suspend, wdt_pm_frequency_change and usbhost_pm_suspend in the m031, m2354 and m480 libraries from int to rt_err_t, to match struct rt_device_pm_ops, whose suspend and frequency_change members became rt_err_t in July 2024. The nuc980 library still declares and defines these callbacks as int (drv_wdt.c lines 62, 64, 93, 141; drv_usbhost.c line 893) and stores them in the same struct inside its RT_USING_PM blocks. With RT_USING_PM enabled the compiler reports an incompatible function-pointer initialization, which stops the build on compilers that reject it and is a warning on others. Behaviour at run time does not change because every callback returns RT_EOK; the shipped NUC980 configurations leave RT_USING_PM off, and the repository does not show whether the original problem was an error or only a warning.

subject: [bsp/gd32]Add GD32VW553H spi support (#11192)
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit is titled "[bsp/gd32]Add GD32VW553H spi support (#11192)" (body: "Add VW553H spi support", "Fix Some Issues"), and both picked hunks only add '#if defined (SOC_SERIES_GD32VW55x)' branches to the RISC-V GD32 driver: a VW55x SPI0 table entry (SPI, RCU_SPI, GPIOA pins 9-11) and a VW55x variant of spi_crc_off/spi_init/spi_enable that takes no peripheral argument. The previous code is kept unchanged under '#else' (apart from one removed blank line), so the behaviour of every chip the driver supported before is the same before and after; this is new-chip support, not a correction of existing behaviour. The ARM GD32 driver's lines are the unchanged generic form: its SPI0 table entry (line 40 onward, SPI0 at line 42, with its own per-pin RCU/port/AF layout) and spi_crc_off(spi_periph), spi_init(spi_periph, &spi_init_struct) and spi_enable(spi_periph) in spi_configure at lines 362-367 match the '#else' branch, and nothing under bsp/gd32/arm refers to GD32VW55x, so there is nothing to carry over.
